title: Areas and Volumes of Similar Figures
seo_title: Sec 3 Areas and volumes of similar figures Worksheets: Free Secondary 3 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
short_title: Areas and volumes of similar figures
standard_text: ratio of areas of similar plane figures; ratio of volumes of similar solids
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 maths worksheets on areas of similar figures and volumes of similar solids: area ratio = (length ratio)², volume ratio = (length ratio)³, mass, capacity and problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Lengths a : b give areas a² : b² and volumes a³ : b³.
key_sub: To go back, take the square root of an area ratio or the cube root of a volume ratio.
body_html:
How it works

If two figures are similar with lengths in the ratio a : b, then

  • areas (including surface areas) are in the ratio a2 : b2;
  • volumes (and masses or capacities of the same material) are in the ratio a3 : b3.

To go back, take the square root of an area ratio or the cube root of a volume ratio to get the length ratio first.

Example

Two similar jugs are 10 cm and 15 cm tall. The small one holds 400 ml. How much does the large one hold?

Length ratio 2 : 3

Volume ratio 8 : 27

400 × 27 ÷ 8

Answer: 1350 ml

Example

The areas of two similar triangles are 16 cm² and 49 cm². Find the ratio of their sides.

√16 : √49

Answer: 4 : 7

Common mistakes

  • Using the length ratio for an area or a volume.
  • Squaring instead of cubing for volume, mass or capacity.
  • Squaring an area ratio to get a length ratio. Take the square root instead.
  • Using AD : DB instead of AD : AB when DE ∥ BC.

faq.q: How are the areas of similar figures related?
faq.a: If the lengths are in the ratio a : b, the areas are in the ratio a² : b².

faq.q: How are the volumes of similar solids related?
faq.a: If the lengths are in the ratio a : b, the volumes are in the ratio a³ : b³. Masses and capacities of the same material follow the same ratio.

faq.q: How do I find a length ratio from a volume ratio?
faq.a: Take the cube root of each part of the volume ratio. For an area ratio, take the square root.

faq.q: Is surface area an area or a volume?
faq.a: An area, so it scales by the square of the length ratio.

items.q: A model car is made to a scale of 1 : 50. The area of the model's windscreen is 30 cm². Find the area of the real windscreen, in m².
items.e: Area scale factor = 502 = 2500. 30 × 2500 = 75 000 cm² = 7.5 m² (1 m² = 10 000 cm²).

items.q: A model car is made to a scale of 1 : 20. The area of the model's windscreen is 40 cm². Find the area of the real windscreen, in m².

items.q: A map has a scale of 1 : 25 000. A park has an area of 8 cm² on the map. Find its actual area in km².
items.e: 1 cm represents 0.25 km, so 1 cm² represents 0.0625 km². 8 × 0.0625 = 0.5 km².

items.q: In △ABC, DE is parallel to BC with D on AB and E on AC. AD : AB = 2 : 3. The area of △ADE is 16 cm². Find the area of △ABC.
items.e: △ADE and △ABC are similar with length ratio 2 : 3, so the area ratio is 4 : 9. 16 × 94 = 36 cm².

items.q: In △ABC, DE is parallel to BC with D on AB and E on AC. AD : DB = 1 : 4. The area of △ADE is 5 cm². Find the area of the trapezium DBCE.
items.e: AD : AB = 1 : 5, so △ADE : △ABC = 1 : 25. △ABC = 125 cm², so DBCE = 125 − 5 = 120 cm².
